# CONT-93 — TEN-GAME MOVEMENT + ACTION + STRATEGY/FARM + 3D EXECUTION MATRIX

This is the final game-focused complement to CONT-88/90 inside master Issue #364. It is NOT a request to merely launch ten APKs or create ten new per-game hacks. Use existing EXEC/game issues and current corpus first; preserve their identities and update them with current-head evidence. Prioritize movement, animation, input/state, stage progression and actual graphics.

## Goal
Test ten distinct game targets spanning:
- 2D real-time motion / physics;
- arcade action / shooter / runner;
- puzzle with animated board/state changes;
- platform/strategy/sandbox progression;
- farming/management-style simulation if a legally usable APK exists;
- Age-of-Empires-like real-time strategy and a true 3D rendering path.

Do not claim all genres are represented if a usable APK is unavailable. If farm/RTS/3D target is not in the corpus, source an open-source/legal x86/x86_64-compatible Android APK, pin exact version and SHA-256, add it to the corpus, and report prerequisite mismatch separately. Do not use ARM-only APKs as evidence of a runtime failure.

## Ten targets (existing corpus/issue anchors first)
1. **Bouncy — com.dozingcatsoftware.bouncy — #21**: 2D physics; move beyond menu/click proof to actual multi-round game-loop state evolution, moving ball/physics and repeatable frame changes.
2. **Mouse Pounce — com.dozingcatsoftware.mouse_pounce — #101**: real-time motion/reaction game; source/pin a valid APK, verify animation cadence, touch-to-state transition and score/round progression.
3. **Asteroids Revenge — com.game.asteroids_revenge — #109 / #366**: 2D action/shooter candidate; establish APK/ABI first, then verify moving sprites, continuous frame loop, projectile/enemy collision or a real action-state change.
4. **FafaRunner — com.chenyifaer.fafarunner — #115**: runner/movement; verify scrolling/world motion, obstacle/state change, touch input and score/game-over path where reachable.
5. **BrickBlast — com.mostafa.brickblast — #106**: arcade action/ball physics; verify paddle/ball movement, collision, score and restart—not a static menu.
6. **TripleMatch — com.sidhant.triplematch — #122**: board/puzzle state; verify actual tile swap/selection, board mutation, match/score or equivalent game-state delta, and animation where the app implements it.
7. **Privacy Friendly Memory — org.secuso.privacyfriendlymemory — #98**: turn-based visual/input control; verify card flip, matched/unmatched state and round completion. This gives a contrasting low-complexity control for event/animation semantics.
8. **Breakout 71 / HTML5 Breakout — existing #94 and evidence chain #353**: WebView/JS game loop; verify that JS timers/RAF, Canvas2D, input and repeated gameplay frames remain functional. Keep this separately classified as the WebView family, not native Android Canvas.
9. **One 3D-capable target — prefer a current corpus APK that actually uses EGL/OpenGL ES (inspect manifest/native libraries/runtime trace; candidates include the existing Space Vertex target in #366 if its exact APK proves this)**: test context creation, shader compile/link, buffers/textures, draw calls, swap/present, depth/blend and moving camera/object. Do not label a 2D canvas game as 3D. If no eligible 3D APK exists, source one with reproducible legal provenance or mark 3D target BLOCKED with the smallest proven prerequisite.
10. **One strategy / farm-management target**: first search the corpus for a real farm/management/RTS APK. If none is usable, source one legal open-source Android strategy/farming title. Prefer a small 2D RTS/factory/farm-management control with visible world, units/entities, selection, placement and progression; if an Age-of-Empires-like APK is selected, record its exact ABI and whether it uses native GLES/Vulkan, Java Canvas or another renderer. Do not claim Age of Empires itself is tested unless that exact artifact is present and pinned. Farming and Age-of-Empires-like strategy are related genre goals but are not interchangeable; report which one the chosen target actually represents.

## Phase 0 — truth and target acquisition
- Read #354, #366, #21, #98, #101, #106, #109, #115, #122, #353 and all linked/current per-app execution records.
- Check the current APK corpus before downloading anything. For each target record package, title, versionCode/versionName, min/target API if available, ABI/native libs, APK SHA-256, source URL/license, and existing issue.
- Re-fetch only artifacts proven corrupt/missing; do not silently replace a corpus APK with a different version.
- Pin current origin/main commit, binary SHA-256 and test harness version. Historical statuses remain HISTORICAL until rerun.

## Phase 1 — common gameplay ladder for every target
For each APK:
1. INSTALL/IDENTITY_OK; ABI compatible.
2. DEX/native initialization reaches actual game screen.
3. First meaningful app-owned pixels (not splash/default background/placeholder).
4. Continuous animation/game loop over a measured time window.
5. Real input through the normal event path.
6. State delta in real game objects/model (not just screenshot hash).
7. Result visible in the next frame: moved entity, changed board, score, collision, selected unit, placed item, etc.
8. Stage/round/game-over/restart when the game exposes it.
9. Three-run reproducibility for any VERIFIED status.

For movement games capture at least 10 frames over time and report frame hashes plus a simple motion metric (changed pixels/bounding-box/object centroid where available). A changing screenshot alone is insufficient if it is flicker or nondeterministic noise. For input, prove event → real listener/DEX method → state delta → visible pixels.

## Phase 2 — cross-family generic graphics/input roots
Trace the first divergence, then cluster at least two distinct APKs per proposed generic fix:
- frame pump, animation invalidation, Choreographer/Handler scheduling and elapsed-time semantics;
- touch coordinates, pointer/action semantics, pressed/move/release, hit-testing and focus;
- Canvas transforms, clipping, alpha, paths, bitmaps, text and draw order;
- RenderNode recording/replay and stale-op accumulation;
- Surface/EGL/GLES context, shader compiler/backend, buffer/texture upload, framebuffer and final present for real 3D target;
- asset/resource loading and density;
- audio/timer/collision only if actual trace identifies it as a blocker.
Use upstream/AOSP/engine source as reference, but local fixture + real APK behavior is the proof. Never add package-name conditions or force an animation/screenshot.

## Phase 3 — farm/RTS and 3D are first-class, not optional wording
- For the farm/strategy target, test world/map drawing, entity updates, selection/placement, camera/scroll/zoom and persistent progression as actually implemented by that APK.
- For the 3D target, prove an actual GLES/EGL path and app-owned rendered geometry. Log context/config, shader compile/link logs, GL errors, buffer/texture sizes, draw counts, swap/present and screenshot provenance. Distinguish Java UI around a 3D game from the actual 3D scene.
- If current runtime lacks shader compilation, test practical CPU/headless options (Mesa llvmpipe or an already-supported software GLES backend) only if available in the project/toolchain; do not claim shader support because GL entry points return success. A shader compile/link + rendered scene is required.
- Age of Empires-like target: verify that the selected APK really contains RTS-like entities/selection/pathing; do not use a turn-based puzzle as a substitute. Farm management and RTS should be separately labelled in the report.

## Phase 4 — measurable result and issue reconciliation
For all ten, return one table:
target | issue | APK SHA | ABI | before state | first missing stage | root ID | source files changed | fixture | after state | movement/state proof | screenshot/trace hashes | 3-run result | regression.
Report counts with distinct APK SHA denominators: NOT_LOADED, WHITE/DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY, REAL_APP_CONTENT, ANIMATED_CONTENT, INTERACTIVE, VERIFIED_GAMEPLAY. Do not combine static render with animated gameplay.

At least four generic fix attempts must reach source + fixture + real-game test, or be explicitly BLOCKED with a concrete dependency proof. At least three unrelated game APKs must improve through generic changes without regressions. Preserve all gates (wall A/B, goldens, negatives, reinstall, privacy, MG-310, MG-150, s82 validator and current graphics/Telegram controls). Update existing issues; do not duplicate them or close them because a menu appears.

## Definition of done
- At least 8/10 targets have a current-head launch verdict; target 10/10 if valid artifacts exist.
- At least 6/10 have real app-owned content; at least 4/10 demonstrate input→state delta→visible result, otherwise state exactly which generic blocker prevents it.
- At least one moving 2D action/physics game proves multiple real frames; one strategy/farm target proves its actual progression interaction; one true 3D target proves rendered geometry and motion.
- If a target is missing/unavailable/ARM-only/proprietary-service blocked, label it honestly and do not count it as runtime failure or success.
- No completion based only on rc=0, no uncaught exception, ViewTree, draw-op count or static screenshot.

# CONT-97 — Ten additional high-fan-out compatibility laws (independent of CONT-96)

Continue inside #364. Do not ask the user to open another issue. These ten tracks are deliberately distinct from CONT-96's Activity/SAX/insets/RecyclerView/resources/SVG/DEX-throughput/Compose/Canvas/native-GLES/input/storage work. First inspect current source, corpus traces and existing registry; map to existing roots and avoid duplicate IDs. Revalidate on current origin/main.

## Ten tracks

### 1. DEX exception-handler boundaries and propagation (P0)
Verify try_item ranges, instruction-PC convention, encoded handlers, catch-all order, subtype matching, nested handlers, rethrow and propagation across interpreted/native invokes and class initialization. Build minimal DEX fixtures for each boundary and prove the correct handler is selected; include a negative case where an unrelated catch must not intercept. Reuse F-NEW-395 history but verify the exact current implementation and do not reopen a fixed root without contrary evidence.

### 2. Class initialization ordering and failure state (P0)
Audit <clinit> exactly-once semantics, superclass/interface initialization order, recursive initialization, initialization failure caching and subsequent access behavior. Test successful, recursive, throwing and retry paths, including static field reads. Trace first divergence and cross-check at least two real APKs.

### 3. Java reflection, method/field resolution and access checks (P0)
Check declared vs inherited members, overload signatures, primitive boxing/unboxing, arrays, bridge/synthetic methods, constructors, accessibility and invocation exceptions. Build table-driven fixtures and verify results against the intended Android/libcore contract. Audit prior ReflectionFactoryImpl/CNFE reports; do not label them blockers unless a real eligible target reaches them.

### 4. Class loaders, multidex and resource identity (P0)
Trace APK DEX enumeration/order, duplicate classes, parent delegation, package-private access, split/dynamic loading where applicable and class identity across loaders. Include multidex fixtures and duplicate-name negatives. Ensure a class from two loaders is not accidentally treated as one identity and that install metadata matches the staged APK generation.

### 5. Android Looper/Handler/message ordering (P1)
Test main-thread identity, post/send ordering, delayed messages under a deterministic clock, removal/cancellation, callback exceptions, queue draining and lifecycle shutdown. Add reproducible fixtures where asynchronous UI state depends on ordering; no arbitrary sleeps or simply extending timeouts. Verify real app traces where evidence supports the contract.

### 6. Thread visibility, monitor and wait/notify semantics (P1)
Audit synchronized methods/blocks, monitor enter/exit, volatile visibility, wait/notify/notifyAll, interruption and deadlock handling in the interpreter/host bridge. Use deterministic stress tests and a bounded liveness test. Do not claim full concurrency correctness from a single pass; document unsupported behavior precisely.

### 7. Intent resolution, component metadata and extras (P1)
Verify explicit/implicit Activity and Service resolution, action/category/data matching, default/exported/enabled flags, launch modes if implemented, extras types, URI payloads, result delivery and back-stack ownership. Build positive/negative fixtures and trace manifest entry→resolver decision→component instance→lifecycle. No package-specific intent routing.

### 8. Configuration changes and saved-state restoration (P1)
Audit orientation/size/density/locale changes, Activity recreation, configuration callbacks, saved instance state, view hierarchy state and restoration ordering. Use a fixture that mutates real app-owned state, recreates the Activity and proves correct restoration without stale object references. Keep unsupported host display modes separate from runtime semantic defects.

### 9. Text layout, font metrics, spans and bidi (P1)
Measure text shaping/layout contracts: font fallback, ascent/descent, baseline, line breaking, spans, ellipsize, includeFontPadding, RTL/bidi and emoji fallback. Compare tree text/layout metrics and screenshot pixels against a pinned golden fixture. Test at least one messaging-style text-heavy app and two unrelated controls; do not fix by hardcoding glyph positions.

### 10. Accessibility/focus navigation and semantic view state (P2)
Audit enabled/disabled/clickable/focusable/selected/pressed state, focus traversal, keyboard navigation, accessibility node identity and state propagation. Build a fixture where focus and selection visibly change and where disabled controls reject input. Connect to existing input tests without duplicating CONT-96's touch/IME work.

- Record current full HEAD, clean/dirty tree, binary SHA-256, registry SHA/count, corpus manifest SHA and toolchain versions.

- For each track: status, source/function, semantic law, first divergence, fixture, positive and negative cases, exact commands/exit codes, before/after output and remaining limitations.

# CONT-98 — Ten more independent Android compatibility law audits and root-fix tracks

This is another execution wave under master Issue #364. It is intentionally separate from CONT-96 and CONT-97. Do not create a new GitHub Issue. Before acting, inspect current origin/main, the latest #364 results, existing root registry and open per-app tickets. Reuse root IDs; avoid duplicate work. All findings from previous comments are historical until revalidated on the current HEAD.

## T1 — APK install transaction, signatures and package metadata consistency (P0)
Trace package parsing and install as one atomic generation: manifest/package identity, version, split/multidex inventory, ABI/native library inventory, resources and DEX must refer to the same APK generation. Test malformed APK, interrupted install, replacement install, rollback and reinstall. Verify failed install leaves the prior installed generation intact and cannot expose mixed V1/V2 metadata. Reconcile with F-NEW-376 rather than duplicating it.

## T2 — Android manifest parsing and component defaults (P0)
Audit manifest namespace handling, application/component attributes, exported/enabled defaults by target SDK, process/task affinity, launch mode, permission declarations, intent filters, aliases and metadata. Create compact fixtures with positive and negative manifests. Trace raw manifest→normalized package model→resolver/lifecycle behavior. Do not infer missing metadata or silently grant undeclared behavior.

## T3 — Broadcast delivery, receiver registration and lifecycle (P1)
Verify manifest-registered and dynamic receivers, action/data/category matching, registration scope, exported/permission checks, ordered vs unordered delivery if supported, duplicate delivery, unregister and process/lifecycle boundaries. Use deterministic sender/receiver fixtures with state-delta evidence and negative authorization cases. Identify precisely which Android broadcast semantics are intentionally unsupported.

## T4 — Service start/bind and foreground-service boundary (P1)
Audit startService/startForegroundService/bindService, service instance identity, onCreate/onStartCommand/onBind/onUnbind/onDestroy order, binder callback identity, start IDs and stop semantics. Use a fixture that records lifecycle order and changes real app-owned state. Separate missing platform policy from incorrect runtime semantics; do not claim foreground-service support if only callbacks are stubbed.

## T5 — ContentResolver/ContentProvider URI contract (P0)
Trace authority resolution, URI parsing/encoding, path matching, MIME lookup, query projection/selection/sort arguments, cursor lifecycle, insert/update/delete, call/openFile and permission grants where implemented. Build an in-memory provider fixture plus file/content URI negatives. Verify query results and caller-visible data; no fake rows. Reuse prior URI/provider backlog entries.

## T6 — Cursor and database contract beyond file existence (P0)
Audit cursor position transitions, column lookup/index errors, NULL/type conversion, close/isClosed, iteration, exceptions and query argument semantics. For SQLite, check transactions, rollback, WAL sidecars, reopen after process restart and concurrent access. Use deterministic fixtures proving row values and commit/rollback behavior; do not equate creating a database file with SQLite compatibility. Reuse existing SQLite root records.

## T7 — PackageManager/ApplicationInfo/PackageInfo truthfulness (P1)
Verify installed-package queries, application metadata, version/code paths, signatures if supported, requested/granted permissions, component lookup, resourcesForApplication and package-not-found behavior. Cross-check every returned field against the actual staged APK and install record. Build two-package isolation tests to prevent one package's metadata or data from leaking into another.

## T8 — Permission checks and app-private boundary (P0)
Audit runtime permission state, manifest permission checks, URI grants, denied operations and app sandbox boundaries. Verify that an ungranted operation fails with the correct observable error and that a granted operation works. Add cross-package read/write denial tests and path traversal/symlink edge cases without weakening existing F-NEW-375/377 protections.

## T9 — Configuration, locale and resource cache invalidation (P1)
Independently test cache invalidation when locale, density, night mode, orientation or package resources change. A cold run and warm run must select equivalent correct resources for the same configuration; changing configuration must not leave stale drawable/string/bitmap objects. Use two configurations and at least two packages, with selected-resource provenance and screenshot/measurement evidence where visible. Connect to CONT-96 resource work without duplicating its root.

## T10 — Process death, restart and durable state recovery (P1)
Trace process termination/recreation, application initialization, saved durable state, pending callback invalidation and cleanup of stale Activity/View references. Use a controlled kill/relaunch fixture with a real persisted mutation; prove durable data survives while process-local state is recreated. Include package isolation and a negative test ensuring callbacks from a dead generation cannot mutate the new UI. Distinguish process lifecycle unsupported by the harness from an implementation bug.

## Per-track acceptance requirements
For every track report:
- Status: IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED / REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE.
- Current root ID(s), related existing issue(s), and why this is not duplicate work.
- Exact source file/function and Android semantic law; first divergence with trace/evidence.
- Minimal positive and negative fixture, exact command and exit code, before/after values.
- Full current HEAD, tree status, binary SHA-256, registry SHA/count, corpus manifest SHA and toolchain version.
- Real APK validation with package/version/ABI/APK SHA; distinguish ABI prerequisite mismatch from runtime failure.
- Three repetitions for claims of stable visible/timing behavior; screenshot SHA/pixel metrics and data provenance when applicable.
- Re-run relevant regression gates and corpus after shared fixes; list regressions and remaining blockers.

## Wave-level delivery target
These are ten execution tracks, not ten documentation-only tasks. Make at least four evidence-backed fix attempts across independent roots where the source and current traces justify changes. If already correct, prove it on current HEAD and mark REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE/ALREADY_FIXED. If blocked, state the exact blocker and evidence, then continue to the next executable track. Prioritize shared fixes that improve at least two unrelated APKs. No package-name hacks, fake data, fake success, or closure of #364 without final evidence review.

# CONT-99 — WHITE-SCREEN EXIT + CORRECT SPATIAL UI RENDERING (layout, images, buttons, text, clipping and final presentation)

This is a focused visual-correctness wave under master Issue #364. It supplements CONT-88..98 and must not create duplicate roots or new issues. The objective is NOT merely to make a screen non-white: each real UI element must appear in its correct position, size, stacking order and own bounds, with correct image/text content and functional interaction. Inspect current origin/main, latest results, root registry and existing #16/#354–#384/per-app issues first. Reuse root IDs. Previous reports must be revalidated on current HEAD.

## Required end-to-end visual pipeline
Trace every target through:
APK/package identity → DEX execution → lifecycle → Activity/Window/decor → content root/view tree → measure → layout → transforms/insets → draw dispatch → clip/save/restore → bitmap/text raster → z-order/composition → correct window/frame present → screenshot capture.
For each failure, identify the FIRST divergence in this chain. “White screen” alone is not a diagnosis.

## Ten execution tracks

### T1 — View measurement and layout contract (P0)
Audit measure specs (EXACTLY/AT_MOST/UNSPECIFIED), measured dimensions, minimum size, layout params, margins, padding, gravity, match/wrap content, nested ViewGroups and requestLayout/invalidation. Create a fixture with a top bar, two columns/rows, nested container, button and image; compare expected tree bounds with actual bounds and screenshot pixels. Find and fix the generic law behind zero-size, full-screen-stretched or overlapping children. Never hardcode per-app coordinates.

### T2 — Parent/child coordinate transforms, density and window insets (P0)
Trace local vs parent vs screen coordinates, translation/scale/rotation, scroll offsets, padding, display density, status/navigation bar insets and decor/content origin. Use a nested fixture with non-zero offsets and density scaling. Assert transformed bounds and hit-test coordinates agree; compare tree→canvas→raster. Check official Telegram and Forkgram where eligible plus two unrelated APKs.

### T3 — ImageView/Drawable sizing, scaleType and image bounds (P0)
Audit ImageView measurement, intrinsic/minimum dimensions, FIT_CENTER/CENTER_CROP/FIT_XY/CENTER_INSIDE/MATRIX behavior, drawable bounds, gravity, tint/state, alpha and density. Test portrait/landscape/square assets in differently sized boxes, including transparent edges and missing images. Prove the image remains within its own view bounds and expected crop/letterbox pixels match; do not resize all images to fill the screen.

### T4 — Button/control bounds, background, state and click target (P0)
Audit Button/TextView/CompoundButton dimensions, background drawable insets, padding, minHeight/minWidth, pressed/disabled/selected state, touch target and clickable/focusable propagation. Test adjacent controls with different widths/heights and non-overlapping hit regions. Show that a tap on one button changes only its real state and that taps outside its bounds do not activate it. A correctly drawn button with a wrong hitbox is not a pass.

### T5 — Text baseline, line wrapping and overlap (P0)
Trace font selection/metrics, ascent/descent, baseline, includeFontPadding, line spacing, maxLines, ellipsize, spans, bidi/RTL, emoji fallback and text measurement vs drawing. Test long/multiline strings beside images and buttons, multiple font sizes, RTL/LTR and clipped text. Verify that the text does not paint outside its measured bounds or cover neighboring controls; compare baseline/line-box metrics and golden pixels.

### T6 — Z-order, elevation, overlays and sibling overlap (P0)
Audit child drawing order, bringToFront, elevation/Z if implemented, foreground/background order, overlays, popup/menu/dialog/window layering and clipping to parent. Build overlapping and non-overlapping sibling fixtures with deterministic expected ordering. Verify the correct element appears on top only where intended, while unrelated siblings retain their own visible regions. Diagnose app-wide overlap as an ordering/transform bug, not a screenshot problem.

### T7 — Canvas save/restore, clipping and invalidation (P0)
Verify save/saveLayer/restore count, clipRect/clipPath, translation/scaling, matrix stack, invalidation region and redraw after state change. Use nested clipping fixtures and negative cases (empty clip, restore underflow, offscreen child). Ensure one child’s clip/transform cannot leak into later siblings. Compare draw trace and raster masks; use existing CONT-96 Canvas/Path work rather than duplicate root records.

### T8 — ScrollView/list/RecyclerView content geometry (P1)
Check viewport vs content size, child layout, scroll range/offset, clipping, item recycling, row bounds and layout after adapter updates. Test a list of real distinct fixture rows with icons, text and buttons; scroll and verify visible rows and tap targets move together. For real APKs, prove content provenance and avoid fabricated rows. Reconcile with existing CONT-96 RecyclerView and input tracks.

### T9 — White/blank/partial-screen forensic classification and recovery (P0)
Re-run the existing white-target batch from CONT-90/current open EXEC issues on current HEAD. For every APK classify first failing stage as lifecycle not reached, root missing, zero-size/offscreen layout, draw dispatch absent, raster empty, wrong window, default background only, frame not presented, timeout/instruction-budget exhausted, resource failure, or genuine app-owned UI. Keep ABI prerequisite mismatch separate. Pick the highest-fan-out confirmed root, fix it, then retest at least two unrelated targets and the affected corpus.

### T10 — Final frame integrity and visual regression harness (P1)
Ensure screenshots come from the correct active window/frame after the runtime's actual present boundary, not from stale frames, overlays or a host-generated substitute. Record frame ID/timestamp, window/root identity, dimensions, screenshot SHA-256, non-background pixel count, connected regions or mask/bounds, and app-content provenance. Add a small golden scene containing separate button/image/text/toolbar/list elements; assert each element's expected bounds and non-overlap tolerance, not only global pixel count. Run three repetitions and cold/warm cases; explain any nondeterminism.

## Required acceptance per target
For every real APK and fixture, capture:
- exact package/version/ABI/APK SHA-256, current commit and binary SHA-256;
- Activity/Window/root identity and lifecycle reached;
- ViewTree parent/child hierarchy, visibility, measured size, laid-out bounds, padding/margins, transform, clip and z-order;
- source/provenance of displayed text, bitmap/drawable and control state;
- event→hit-tested target→callback→real state delta for any interaction claim;
- screenshot SHA-256, image dimensions, meaningful pixel/bounds/overlap metrics and three-run stability;
- first divergence, root ID reused, exact source/function changed, fixture positive/negative results, commands and exit codes;
- corpus/regression gates and remaining blockers.

## Wave-level implementation target
This is a visual-correctness implementation wave, not documentation-only triage. Attempt at least four evidence-backed fixes across independent root families where current traces justify them. Prefer generic changes that improve multiple unrelated APKs. If a candidate is already correct, prove it with a current-head fixture and mark REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE/ALREADY_FIXED. If blocked, state the precise blocker and continue. No package-specific branches, hardcoded coordinates, app-painted overlays, fake content, forced screenshots, “non-white means pass”, or closure of #364 without review.

## CONT-109 — CHEETAH SPEED × ELEPHANT-SCALE EXECUTION
### 30-track batch mission: source-first discovery, shared-root fixes, verified cross-app results

This is a continuation of **Issue #364**, not a replacement issue and not permission to create another pile of unverified findings. Read the full current #364 thread first, especially CONT-98 through CONT-108, reconcile every claimed fix against current `origin/main`, the source tree, root registry, and existing evidence. Continue from the actual current baseline; do not assume a SHA or registry count from an old report.

## Mission rule: move like a cheetah, carry like an elephant
- **Cheetah speed:** use fast source-first scans, targeted grep/indexing, call-graph and exception-path tracing, existing tests/harnesses, and parallel independent investigations. Do not spend hours decoding APKs when the source already exposes the likely contract.
- **Elephant-scale delivery:** batch related failures into shared semantic/root-cause families, implement reusable runtime fixes, and retest multiple affected apps/games per fix. Avoid one-title-at-a-time patches and app-specific hacks.
- **Do not optimize for the number of comments, findings, or labels.** Optimize for verified root causes fixed, affected titles improved, regressions avoided, and evidence reproducible.
- Existing CONT-105 already reported a 29-unit batch. Therefore, merely claiming “large batch” is not progress. This mission requires explicit cross-track dependency grouping, source-backed solution proposals, real code changes where justified, and measured cross-app impact.

## First: establish truth
1. Record current local HEAD, `origin/main`, working-tree changes, build binary SHA-256/SHA-16, build command, corpus/registry counts, and evidence paths. Preserve user changes; never reset or overwrite unrelated work.
2. Read the existing #364 comments and linked evidence, including CONT-98–108. Reconcile claims for F-NEW-445–453 and prior roots against current source and tests. Do not re-add existing issues under new IDs.
3. For every candidate, identify: affected app/game and ABI; first divergence; source file/function; violated Android/runtime semantic contract; reusable fix proposal; test that would falsify the hypothesis; status.
4. Use statuses exactly: `IMPLEMENTED`, `TESTED`, `OBSERVED`, `PARTIAL`, `BLOCKED`, `PENDING`, `SUPERSEDED`. “Implemented” is not “tested”; a screenshot alone is not proof of semantic correctness.

## 30 investigation tracks — run as a coordinated batch
For each track, search existing roots first, inspect source before expensive APK work, and record concrete app/game examples. Tracks may be grouped and run in parallel when independent; merge fixes by shared root cause.

1. **Telegram startup / first divergence:** trace the first failed or divergent event from process entry through DEX/framework/lifecycle; close startup death families only with trace-backed proof.
2. **Telegram real UI completion:** distinguish a genuinely constructed, measured, interactive UI from placeholder, blue/blank fallback, or merely non-crashing startup.
3. **Compose drawing / AndroidCanvas bridge:** trace Compose-to-framework drawing, canvas object identity, draw commands, and missing bridge methods.
4. **Chess toolbar/content sizing:** revalidate F-NEW-448 against current source, evidence, and real view-tree dimensions; find other apps affected by the same contract.
5. **n2.r / MessageInfo metadata:** revalidate F-NEW-449; trace metadata/class-shape assumptions and affected call sites.
6. **Lazy singleton / class initialization:** revalidate F-NEW-445/446/447/452; test initialization order, cached state, and cold-vs-warm behavior.
7. **ConstraintLayout measured dimensions:** revalidate F-NEW-451/F-NEW-453; verify the reported keypad subtree loss and ensure the solver fix generalizes beyond one screen.
8. **View measurement/layout:** parent specs, measure state, exact/at-most/unspecified modes, layout bounds, requestLayout/invalidation, nested subtrees.
9. **ImageView/drawable:** scaleType, intrinsic size, bounds, density, padding, clipping, stateful drawables.
10. **TextView/text layout:** font metrics, baseline, line breaking, spans, gravity, ellipsizing, compound drawables and measured size.
11. **Button/input controls:** hit targets, clickable/focusable state, touch dispatch, listener invocation, text/state mutation and visual feedback.
12. **Density/transforms/insets:** dp/px conversion, matrix transforms, translations, window/system insets, coordinate conversion and clipping.
13. **Resources/TypedArray:** revalidate F-NEW-450; resource lookup, theme/style resolution, typed values, recycling/lifetime and configuration qualifiers.
14. **ContentProvider/URI:** authority resolution, URI parsing, MIME/type contracts, query/insert/update/delete and permission behavior.
15. **Cursor/SQLite/data contracts:** cursor position/lifetime, column lookup, null/type semantics, close behavior, query results and persistence.
16. **Broadcast/lifecycle delivery:** registration, filtering, delivery ordering, receiver lifecycle, permission and callback semantics.
17. **Activity/task lifecycle:** create/start/resume/pause/stop/recreate/back/task-stack and saved-state transitions.
18. **Reflection/runtime metadata:** declared/inherited members, modifiers, inner-class flags, method/field lookup, access and exception behavior.
19. **DEX/type semantics:** invoke kinds, register/type compatibility, arrays, exceptions, verifier/runtime boundary and first-divergence tracing.
20. **JNI/native ABI:** prioritize runnable x86/x86_64 APKs. Classify ARM/ARM64-only cases as ABI prerequisites unless evidence proves a separate runtime defect; never count an ABI mismatch as a runtime fix.
21. **Filesystem/preferences/persistence:** per-package sandbox paths, cold start vs warm start, preferences/database/files, reinstall and data-retention semantics.
22. **Handler/Looper/async callbacks:** queue ordering, delayed messages, thread affinity, callback delivery and shutdown behavior.
23. **RecyclerView/adapter/scrolling:** adapter counts, bind/create/recycle, item bounds, scrolling, notifications and nested layout.
24. **SVG/graphics/clipping:** path/paint semantics, alpha, clipping, transforms, antialiasing, image decode and drawable-to-canvas paths.
25. **Window/surface/render backend:** distinguish software/GL/window failures; never treat blank or solid-color fallback as successful rendering.
26. **Corpus-wide clustering:** cluster at least 200 eligible titles, or the largest actually available eligible subset, by shared source/runtime root. Report exact denominator and exclusions.
27. **Existing backlog reconciliation:** inspect CONT-89/92/93 and F-NEW-381 plus related open roots; close only when evidence satisfies the original acceptance criteria, otherwise update with concrete blockers.
28. **Cross-app root-cause mining:** investigate at least five concrete app/game cases in this pass. For each, write “This app/game fails because X; the shared runtime fix is Y; these other titles should benefit; this test can disprove the hypothesis.”
29. **Harness / false-positive audit:** check determinism, repeatability, stale binaries, fallback screenshots, silent exception swallowing, flaky state, and whether the test really exercises the claimed code path.
30. **Integration / final adjudication:** combine safe fixes, run targeted tests plus relevant regression batteries, reconcile root registry and evidence, and report remaining blockers honestly.

## Required batch execution
- Start by making a compact dependency map and grouping tracks into shared root-cause clusters. Avoid 30 isolated mini-investigations.
- Investigate at least five concrete app/game cases before finalizing proposals; where evidence supports it, aim for 10–15 meaningful work units with terminal verdicts in one cycle (20+ is a stretch target, not a reason to lower proof standards).
- For every selected root, provide a **source-level proposed fix** before or alongside implementation: file/function, current incorrect behavior, intended semantic law, code change, tests, affected titles. Do not stop at “investigate”, an issue label, or a generic request.
- Implement shared framework/runtime fixes when the same contract explains multiple failures. Avoid title-specific conditionals unless the Android contract genuinely requires them.
- Run focused tests first, then the relevant regression suite. Where feasible, perform three repeat runs and cold/warm comparisons. Include a negative/control case when useful.
- If a hypothesis is disproved, record the falsifying evidence and mark it `SUPERSEDED` or `BLOCKED` with a reason rather than forcing a fix.
- Do not claim full Telegram compatibility from launch alone. Demonstrate actual content, correct ViewTree/provenance, bounds, state changes, input interaction and persistence where applicable.

## Minimum evidence for each claimed fix
Include:
1. Root ID and status; affected app/game title/package and ABI.
2. Exact source paths/functions and the semantic contract being repaired.
3. Before/after first-divergence trace or runtime event sequence.
4. ViewTree/node provenance and measured bounds where UI is involved; show the state transition and click/input target where interaction is claimed.
5. Reproduction command, test name, exit result and repeat count.
6. Screenshot artifact path plus hash, **paired with semantic/runtime evidence**; screenshots or PIL/PNG checks alone do not prove correctness.
7. Binary identity and source HEAD used for the test; confirm tests ran against the rebuilt intended binary.
8. Regression/A-B result, affected titles improved, and any regressions or limitations.
9. Registry/evidence changes and links/paths to durable artifacts.

## Final response format
Return a compact ledger, not a victory paragraph:
- **Baseline:** local HEAD, origin/main, dirty paths, binary hash, corpus/registry count.
- **Batch:** tracks attempted / completed / blocked; meaningful work units with terminal verdicts.
- **At least five app/game cases:** each as problem → source/root cause → reusable fix → evidence → status.
- **Root ledger:** existing IDs reused/closed/refreshed, genuinely new roots only, duplicates rejected.
- **Tests:** commands, pass/fail counts, repeat runs, negative controls, regressions, binary identity.
- **Impact:** actual titles whose runtime behavior improved, and what remains unproven.
- **Commit/push:** commit SHA and confirmation that remote contains it; never claim pushed unless verified.
- **Next blockers:** highest-impact unresolved roots, each with a source-backed next step.

**Acceptance gate:** A list of 30 ideas, 30 new issue IDs, a green test count without test identity, or “done” without evidence does not satisfy this mission. Success means shared runtime laws fixed, multiple real apps/games measurably improved, evidence reproducible from the stated source/binary, and the existing #364 registry kept consistent.

## CONT-110 — SOURCE-RESEARCHED WHITE-SCREEN + REAL TELEGRAM UI REPAIR PLAN
### 50 concrete tasks, proposed semantic fixes, and falsifiable tests — continue in this issue

I independently inspected the current repository's existing evidence before writing this plan: `docs/WHITE_SCREEN_LOADING_ROOTS.md`, `docs/LOADING_FAILURE_DIAGNOSTICS.md`, `docs/WORKING_APP_LOADING_EXPLANATIONS.md`, Issue [#366 differential execution](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/366), Telegram transfer/issues [#357](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/357), [#359](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/359), [#363](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/363), and the broad black/white/partial audit [#372](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/372). I am not treating these historical reports as independently reproduced current-HEAD tests; the coder must revalidate them against the current source and binary.

## The diagnosis: why screens are white or Telegram is incomplete

The existing evidence already disproves the idea that all white screens are APK/file-loading bugs. The loading docs classify Sudoku and WhatsApp as `WINDOW_ROOT` / content-root-chain failures, not byte-loading failures; the Telegram settings face loads assets and preferences, while its wrong screen is an `ACTIVITY_NAVIGATION` / lifecycle problem. The loading probe's stream/FD/asset/persistence cases were separately covered by synthetic probes. Therefore, do not spend another cycle re-fixing file APIs when the first divergence is higher in the UI pipeline.

For Telegram, prior work got from startup exceptions to a constructed/measured tree and a real login frame, but the remaining gap is end-to-end UI semantics: fragment attachment/navigation, country picker and input, actual drawable/background painting, rows/ViewHolder creation, Compose/custom drawing capture, and final-frame truth. Earlier evidence explicitly calls out RecyclerView rows not being built, a country-picker fragment whose `onFragmentCreate/createView` execute but whose tree does not attach, a country-field child that measures 0×0 on a later pass, and grey placeholder bottom-grid rows. Revalidate each; do not assume all remain unfixed.

**Execution rule:** first-divergence trace → source function → AOSP/AndroidX semantic law → smallest generic fix → falsifiable probe → current-HEAD app run → cross-family regression. Existing root IDs must be reused. Do not create 50 new root IDs by default.

---

# Batch A — stop white/blank screens at the earliest missing stage (tasks 1–12)

### 01 — Make the first-divergence trace mandatory per frame
**Proposal:** centralize stage markers for process/component resolution, lifecycle, window/content root, ViewTree attach, measure, layout, draw, surface/buffer, present, capture. Emit the first missing expected event, not just the final exception.
**Test:** same run must classify known Sudoku/WhatsApp faces as window/content-root class when current evidence still reproduces, and a synthetic decode failure as a loading class.

### 02 — Revalidate Sudoku's WINDOW_ROOT diagnosis
**Proposal:** trace `Activity.setContentView`/content-parent → decor/window root attachment → traversal scheduling. Fix missing generic root attachment or traversal dispatch only if that is the first divergence.
**Test:** ViewTree has the real app's nodes, attached root dimensions >0, draw occurs, app-owned pixels appear; 3 cold runs.

### 03 — Revalidate WhatsApp's window/content chain separately
**Proposal:** do not copy the Sudoku diagnosis without proof. Compare Activity lifecycle, window root, child attach, and app draw against a working View-based app.
**Test:** first divergence documented; if APK corruption/ABI/environment is the real blocker, classify it honestly instead of calling it a renderer bug.

### 04 — Separate loading, lifecycle, layout, draw, present, and capture verdicts
**Proposal:** make the classifier return one explicit earliest failed stage with evidence references; keep file I/O and rendering verdicts independent.
**Test:** feed it one known synthetic failure from each stage and assert the distinct expected classification.

### 05 — Audit every “successful blank” / fail-soft path
**Proposal:** search for default null/zero/empty returns, swallowed exceptions, forced success exit codes, placeholder-only output, and stale-frame reuse. Replace only where the Android contract requires a real result or explicit failure.
**Test:** unsupported API produces a traceable honest failure, never a fake successful blank frame.

### 06 — Distinguish absent tree from tree-not-attached
**Proposal:** expose separate counters for created nodes, attached nodes, measured nodes, laid-out nodes, draw-dispatched nodes, and nodes that contribute to the frame.
**Test:** a synthetic unattached subtree cannot be misreported as a draw failure; an attached but zero-sized subtree is classified as geometry.

### 07 — Prove the actual installed APK is being executed
**Proposal:** bind every run to installed package identity + installed base.apk hash + APK entry provenance; remove source-file fallback ambiguity.
**Test:** hide/move the original APK after install and confirm the same installed identity and content run.

### 08 — Audit the full ViewRoot/traversal scheduling contract
**Proposal:** compare MiniAndroid's traversal order with AOSP ViewRootImpl: layout requested → measure/layout → draw → frame presentation; ensure invalidation and requestLayout schedule a traversal at the correct boundary.
**Test:** changing a real view's state then calling invalidate/requestLayout changes the expected bounds/frame without a forced extra frame.

### 09 — Verify final-frame freshness
**Proposal:** attach frame sequence IDs/timestamps to draw ops, framebuffer updates and screenshots; reject screenshots of the previous frame.
**Test:** a tap changes state and yields a new frame ID and hash; a deliberately stale capture fails the gate.

### 10 — Overdraw/debug placeholder audit
**Proposal:** keep debug surfaces strictly opt-in and distinguish capture gaps from genuinely empty `onDraw`; never let placeholder fills count as app content.
**Test:** real empty custom View stays transparent; a known canvas capture gap is marked CAPTURE_GAP, not REAL_APP_UI.

### 11 — Add a minimal differential nine-app run from #366
**Proposal:** use the existing 4-working + 5-white design; reuse OpenCalc, uNote, MicroTimer, Chess if still green, and select five currently genuinely white apps from current corpus.
**Test:** one matrix row per APK includes source/install SHA, lifecycle, ViewTree, layout/draw, first divergence and screenshot hash; three-run subset as #366 requires.

### 12 — Use a source-first decision tree before touching storage
**Proposal:** if first missing stage is before any file/resource request, block storage changes for that case; if stream/decode is the first divergence, use the existing loading laws and probe.
**Test:** report lists the observed first missing event and shows why the selected subsystem is causal.

# Batch B — Telegram: turn a clean launch into a complete, interactive UI (tasks 13–27)

### 13 — Revalidate the login Activity → Fragment → Window chain
**Proposal:** trace the real FragmentManager transaction through fragment creation, view creation, view attachment and transition completion. Do not equate `createView()` with an attached fragment.
**Test:** fragment identity exists in manager, root view is attached once, expected lifecycle callbacks occur in order, visible bounds are nonzero.

### 14 — Fix the country-picker fragment attachment frontier
**Existing report:** #363 says picker fragment `au` reaches `onFragmentCreate/createView` but its tree does not attach.
**Proposal:** trace the first missing manager/transaction/parent attachment step; implement that generic Fragment transaction/commit/animation contract, not a Telegram branch.
**Test:** tap country row → picker root attached → country rows visible → back returns to login; state survives 3 runs.

### 15 — Revalidate the country-field second-pass 0×0 child
**Proposal:** trace the second measure pass, parent MeasureSpec, LayoutParams, visibility and late child attachment. Invalidate stale DEX-measured dimensions when parent constraints change; never allow stale 0×0 to override a valid native measurement.
**Test:** field and children have expected nonzero bounds and remain stable across repeated traversal.

### 16 — Complete phone-number input semantics
**Proposal:** wire EditText text storage, input dispatch, focus, cursor/selection, input type and text-change callbacks as one coherent contract.
**Test:** type digits; DEX getter returns exactly typed text; cursor and visible text agree; clear/backspace works.

### 17 — Complete the login button's real background pipeline
**Existing report:** #363 calls out programmatic GradientDrawable and `View.setBackground` being a no-op.
**Proposal:** make `setBackground(Drawable)` retain the receiver's actual drawable object, preserve bounds/state, and dispatch its drawing through the normal renderer. Implement GradientDrawable shape/color/corner/radius semantics needed by callers.
**Test:** real button background and rounded blue FAB appear from the app-created drawable; no pixel-specific overlay.

### 18 — Revalidate the login banner geometry
**Proposal:** find why the low-power banner was reported as 1028×1920 and compare parent/child specs, weight, margins and wrap-content behavior with AOSP.
**Test:** banner has content-sized bounds and does not push other login controls below the screen.

### 19 — Revalidate status-bar height and insets
**Proposal:** route status-bar/window insets through one canonical source and apply them once; do not mix physical pixels with dp or duplicate top padding.
**Test:** login and picker bounds stay correct at multiple display densities and with/without fullscreen.

### 20 — Fix login button and content below-fold placement
**Proposal:** use actual parent constraints, weight distribution and bottom anchoring rather than hard-coded screenshot coordinates.
**Test:** button lies inside viewport and responds to a tap at its measured hit rectangle on at least two viewport sizes.

### 21 — Rebuild the Telegram dialog-list ViewHolder path
**Existing report:** #363 says DB data exists but RecyclerView holders are not built.
**Proposal:** trace adapter item count → createViewHolder → bindViewHolder → child attach → measure/layout → draw. Implement missing generic RecyclerView/adapter contract at the first divergence.
**Test:** visible rows correspond to real adapter/database items; scrolling reuses/rebinds holders correctly; no fabricated rows.

### 22 — Fix dialog row click → chat navigation
**Proposal:** trace pointer dispatch through item hit testing, adapter position, stable item identity, data handoff and Fragment transaction.
**Test:** tapping row N opens the matching chat, not a neighboring row; back returns to the same scroll position.

### 23 — Revalidate login → main fragment transition
**Proposal:** verify lifecycle callbacks and frame invalidation across fragment replacement; prevent the outgoing full-screen sibling from remaining visible.
**Test:** successful login/transition produces the expected new root and frame, with no stale blank/white intermediate stuck state.

### 24 — Revalidate drawer open/close and Settings navigation
**Proposal:** inspect touch dispatch, drawer offset/translation, scrim drawing, z-order and fragment routing.
**Test:** open, close, and settings taps change state and visible frame; no invisible click targets.

### 25 — Make asynchronous UI work visible to traversal
**Proposal:** check Handler/Looper callback queue, thread affinity, posted layout work, animation callbacks and frame invalidation. Do not run UI callbacks on the wrong queue or drop pending tasks.
**Test:** a queued UI mutation deterministically updates the next eligible frame; cancellation and lifecycle-stop cases are tested.

### 26 — Revalidate theme/style/TypedArray on actual Telegram widgets
**Proposal:** trace each missing attribute from styleable ID → theme/style resolution → TypedArray value → drawable/text consumer. Avoid replacing all missing attrs with arbitrary defaults.
**Test:** selected theme attributes match the app's resource values; light/dark theme probe plus a second app using the same API.

### 27 — Complete the user journey as separate gates
**Proposal:** create stepwise gates for intro → phone input → country picker → code screen → main list → open chat → type/send. Keep unsupported network/TLS/backend behavior separate from local UI execution.
**Test:** each step has input event, callback, state delta, resulting ViewTree and frame evidence; do not claim end-to-end messaging if server/native/network prerequisites block it.

# Batch C — shared View/layout/text/draw laws (tasks 28–38)

### 28 — Revalidate F-NEW-451/F-NEW-453 ConstraintLayout law
**Proposal:** preserve the reported rule: a valid native measured size must not be overwritten by stale invalid DEX 0×0 under demanding EXACTLY specs; clear invalid measurement provenance during native takeover.
**Test:** keypad case plus at least two independent ConstraintLayout targets; compare measured dimensions, subtree count and frame hashes.

### 29 — Close F-NEW-448 only if toolbar content sizing is truly fixed
**Proposal:** trace the chess toolbar/content/min-height chain; inspect parent MeasureSpec, child min-height, margins and late measurement.
**Test:** Chess and two other toolbar/content layouts have correct non-overlapping bounds, not just a golden hash.

### 30 — Close F-NEW-449 only with a general metadata law
**Proposal:** trace n2.r / MessageInfo class metadata and exact field/method/modifier assumptions. Fix the generic class-shape/reflection contract if proven; do not hard-code class names.
**Test:** metadata probe covers the failing shape and a negative/unrelated class; Telegram's caller reaches the correct method/field.

### 31 — Audit `View.setVisibility` and child pruning
**Proposal:** separate INVISIBLE (measured/layout semantics as AOSP requires) from GONE (excluded from layout); ensure renderer pruning does not incorrectly remove nodes based on a stale state.
**Test:** three-state probe for VISIBLE/INVISIBLE/GONE checks node presence, dimensions, draw ops and sibling positioning.

### 32 — Audit MeasureSpec and resolveSizeAndState full tables
**Proposal:** compare EXACTLY/AT_MOST/UNSPECIFIED behavior, MATCH_PARENT/WRAP_CONTENT, padding, margins and measured-state bits against AOSP source.
**Test:** table-driven parent/child combinations, including zero-sized parent and nonzero EXACTLY constraints; add metamorphic assertions.

### 33 — Audit LinearLayout weight and remaining-space allocation
**Proposal:** validate the known h=0, weight=1 parent remaining-space distribution and make it consistent for vertical/horizontal orientations, margins and padding.
**Test:** two weighted siblings divide remaining space according to weights; total bounds equal available content area.

### 34 — Audit late child attachment/requestLayout
**Proposal:** adding/removing a child invalidates parent measurement/layout at the correct lifecycle point; derive new specs from parent, never from the child's stale unmeasured rect.
**Test:** attach a child after first layout and verify it is measured, positioned and drawn in the next traversal.

### 35 — Audit TextView/TextShaper/StaticLayout end-to-end
**Proposal:** compare measured text line boxes, baseline, line count, font metrics, spans, ellipsizing, gravity and actual glyph paint; preserve exact descriptor overloads and real text objects.
**Test:** multilingual/RTL/long-line probes plus Telegram title, button label and an independent app; bounds and visible glyph pixels agree.

### 36 — Audit Canvas call capture versus actual draw dispatch
**Proposal:** keep three facts separate: draw method executed, canvas calls issued, and operations successfully captured. Use the calls-seen/provenance counters to locate the missing bridge.
**Test:** a view with zero draw calls is transparent; a view with calls but zero captured ops is CAPTURE_GAP and cannot pass as visually verified.

### 37 — Audit Drawable bounds/state propagation
**Proposal:** ensure setBounds, intrinsic dimensions, state changes, alpha, tint, level and callback invalidation flow from the drawable to the consumer view.
**Test:** stateful selector changes on pressed/selected state; bounds match view content rect; draw occurs only within clip.

### 38 — Audit elevation, clipping and sibling order
**Proposal:** compare translationZ/elevation, clipChildren/clipToPadding, scroll offsets and drawing order. Remove debug overpaint, but don't replace legitimate app surfaces.
**Test:** overlapping two-view probe verifies deterministic draw order and clipping; Surface/GL target remains unaffected.

# Batch D — Compose, WebView, native, surfaces and game rendering (tasks 39–45)

### 39 — Dooz Compose first divergence, not a blanket Compose rewrite
**Proposal:** trace app-bundled Compose Runtime through Composer/SlotTable/Applier/ComposeNode → LayoutNode → measure/layout/draw. Revalidate the existing F-NEW-271 / recomposition-starvation hypotheses and current R-NEW-347/345 family.
**Test:** two independent Compose targets; demonstrate composition state changes, attached layout nodes and real content pixels. A ComposeView wrapper outline is not content.

### 40 — Compose state/recomposition scheduling
**Proposal:** find whether state writes invalidate the correct composition scope and whether the frame scheduler consumes invalidations; avoid repeatedly reporting success because wrapper drawing occurred.
**Test:** state A→B updates real text/layout/pixels in the next expected frame; unchanged state does not cause an infinite redraw loop.

### 41 — Compose Canvas / AndroidCanvas bridge
**Proposal:** map each actual app-issued draw operation through the app's Compose canvas abstraction into MiniAndroid's CanvasShadow; preserve object identity, transforms, clipping and paint.
**Test:** a known Compose Canvas scene matches expected shapes/text/clip and records calls-seen == captured ops for supported operations.

### 42 — WebView/HTML5 white-screen execution ladder
**Proposal:** trace WebView creation → HTML load → DOM ready → JS execution → requestAnimationFrame/game loop → canvas/WebGL surface → composite. Do not treat page load or a WebView shell as game content.
**Test:** use #353's Breakout as a reference; prove a changing game state/frame sequence and input response; separate JS errors from graphics/capture failure.

### 43 — SurfaceView/GL compositing preservation
**Proposal:** inspect surface lifecycle, buffer acquisition/presentation, synchronization/fence behavior and final composite; never let a generic View fallback overwrite or replace a working surface path.
**Test:** flappycow/known Surface-family control remains byte-stable or intentionally rebaselined with explanation after View fixes.

### 44 — Native/JNI ABI truth for Telegram and games
**Proposal:** report APK ABI and available runtime native bridge before launch; do not classify ARM-only native code as a View rendering bug. Verify each JNI symbol's descriptor, return type and error behavior.
**Test:** x86/x86_64-native targets prioritized; unsupported ABI fails honestly before UI claims, and supported native call is proven end-to-end.

### 45 — Fonts, bitmap decode and image consumer provenance
**Proposal:** trace resource/file bytes → decoder → Bitmap/Drawable identity → consumer → draw op. Distinguish missing bytes, decode failure, invisible/zero bounds and capture gaps.
**Test:** Telegram logo/icon and an independent image-heavy app show the real decoded asset with dimensions/hash/provenance; placeholder images cannot pass.

# Batch E — corpus, instrumentation, and closure discipline (tasks 46–50)

### 46 — Audit the grey bottom-grid rows (`zr`) in Telegram
**Existing report:** #363 says the lower grid rows remain grey placeholders (about 11.86% of the frame in that report).
**Proposal:** trace each row's producer, data/model state, child construction, drawable/background, measured bounds and canvas calls. Determine whether grey comes from a missing real child, absent data, unsupported drawable, or capture gap.
**Test:** real row nodes and content are present; if no data exists on a no-SIM/no-account path, represent that state honestly rather than inventing content.

### 47 — Fix the remaining country-row / picker journey after revalidation
**Proposal:** join the picker attachment, country list adapter, click selection and field update into one tested generic path; avoid faking SIM/country data.
**Test:** tap country row → visible picker → select country → field updates; test no-SIM and no-network negative cases separately.

### 48 — Cluster the 200-title corpus by first missing semantic stage
**Proposal:** classify each eligible title into install/ABI, lifecycle/component, root/attach, resource, measure/layout, text/draw, Compose, WebView, Surface/native, input/state, persistence or capture. Cluster by shared source primitive before choosing fixes.
**Test:** report exact denominator, exclusions, duplicate clusters and at least five actual app/game cases with source-backed shared-fix proposals.

### 49 — Add one fast regression suite per root family
**Proposal:** create minimal deterministic probes for window-root attachment, fragment attach, MeasureSpec, weighted layout, drawable background, TextView paint, RecyclerView bind, Compose recomposition, WebView JS/canvas, and Surface composite. Keep probes cheap and reuse them in the full corpus.
**Test:** each probe fails on a deliberately injected wrong law, passes on current fix, then the existing three game anchors and app goldens are checked.

### 50 — Deliver a source-backed closeout ledger and stop duplicating old requests
**Proposal:** reconcile every task with root_registry/canonical worklist and existing #364/366/372/357–363 evidence. Reuse root IDs; new ID only for a proven genuinely new semantic law.
**Test:** final table has task → source/function → semantic law → current divergence → proposed/implemented fix → tests → affected apps → evidence SHA → status. Verify current HEAD and origin/main; no unsupported “fully compatible” claim.

---

## Priority order for fastest real improvement
1. **P0: tasks 01–12** — make first divergence reliable and stop misclassifying UI failures as loading failures.
2. **P0: tasks 13–24** — close Telegram's actual attachment/navigation/input/background/RecyclerView paths.
3. **P1: tasks 28–38** — shared measurement, text, drawable and canvas laws with high fan-out.
4. **P1: tasks 39–45** — separate Compose/WebView/Surface/native families and fix their first missing bridge.
5. **P1: tasks 46–50** — remaining visible Telegram frontier, corpus cluster, cheap regression and honest closure.

## What counts as success
Do not merely tick 50 boxes. First identify at least five real failing apps/games and their actual first divergence; group them into shared semantic roots; implement the smallest generic fixes that are proven; show before/after state, ViewTree, geometry, draw provenance and frame hash; run relevant golden regressions and repeat selected targets three times. If a proposed root is disproved, record the falsifying trace and do not implement it.

The existing docs and prior reports are research leads, not a substitute for checking the current source and current HEAD. Keep this execution in Issue #364, update its ledger/worklog/evidence, and leave every unproven Telegram journey step PARTIAL/BLOCKED/PENDING rather than calling the UI complete.
