body:
## CONT-110 — WHITE SCREEN + INCOMPLETE TELEGRAM UI: 50 SOURCE-BACKED WORK ITEMS
### Assistant research addendum — diagnose first divergence, fix shared laws, recover real UI

This is a **continuation note on #364**, not a new issue and not permission to duplicate the existing white-screen/Telegram campaigns. I inspected the current #364 thread and these existing repository artifacts:
- `docs/WHITE_SCREEN_LOADING_ROOTS.md`
- `docs/LOADING_FAILURE_DIAGNOSTICS.md`
- `docs/WORKING_APP_LOADING_EXPLANATIONS.md`
- #366, “DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION — Why 4 apps work and 5 installed apps stay white”
- #372, “SUPPLEMENTARY DEEP ROOT-CAUSE CLOSEOUT — 330-point black/white/partial/load audit”
- Telegram knowledge transfer #357–#363, especially #359 and #363
- existing CONT-98–CONT-109 reports, including the ConstraintLayout/keypad fix F-NEW-453.

**Important baseline finding:** the repository already documents that several white targets are NOT file-loading failures. Its documented first-missing stages include WINDOW_ROOT, VIEW_BIND/content-parent, ACTIVITY_NAVIGATION and COMPOSE; synthetic file/stream/FD probes already cover a different failure class. Do not re-open fixed loading laws without a current counterexample. Also, the prior Telegram reports show meaningful progress (clean execution, a real tree, some real text), but they explicitly leave navigation, content/rows, draw capture, geometry and interaction gaps. Treat old evidence as a hypothesis to revalidate against current HEAD, not proof that the present build still behaves identically.

## Research-backed technical frame

AOSP's View contract says the parent supplies MeasureSpecs (EXACTLY/AT_MOST/UNSPECIFIED); `requestLayout()` schedules measurement/layout, while `invalidate()` schedules drawing. A child with wrong specs, stale measured dimensions, or no invalidation can therefore leave a valid-looking tree visually empty. Source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/HEAD/core/java/android/view/View.java

AOSP's ViewRootImpl performs a traversal/measure pass; Compose is a separate composition → layout → draw pipeline and recomposition depends on state observation. Do not treat “Compose function executed” or “ComposeView exists” as proof that the final frame contains Compose content. Sources:
- https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/ViewRootImpl.java
- https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/lifecycle
- https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/quick-guides/content/video/debugging-recomposition

These sources establish the semantic contracts; they do NOT prove a particular current MiniAndroid bug. Every candidate below must be matched to current MiniAndroid source and a reproducer before changing code.

## 50 tasks in one coordinated batch

For every task, first search the current root registry/worklist and existing #366/#372/#357–#363 evidence. Classify as ALREADY_COVERED / SAME_ROOT_NEW_EVIDENCE / NEW_SUBLAW / NEW_ROOT / NOT_APPLICABLE. Only implement a new fix after a current-source divergence is reproduced. Group tasks by common root and do not create 50 isolated patches.

### A. One fast, authoritative diagnosis pipeline (1–8)

**01 — Refresh baseline identity.** Record current origin/main HEAD, working-tree state, build command, binary hash, exact APK SHA and installed package/base.apk identity for every tested target. Never mix old screenshot/evidence with a new binary.

**02 — Run the existing white-vs-working matrix first.** Continue #366, not a duplicate matrix. Revalidate at least four known working controls and five genuinely white/blank installed APKs; replace targets that no longer reproduce and state why.

**03 — Produce one stage trace per target.** Instrument the same ordered path: package/component resolution → Application/Activity lifecycle → setContentView/Compose/WebView → window/root attachment → ViewTree → measure → layout → draw → framebuffer/present → capture.

**04 — Emit FIRST_DIVERGENCE automatically.** For each stage, record expected observable, actual observable, source caller, object identity, time/frame, and result. The earliest missing observable—not the last visible symptom—is the primary diagnosis.

**05 — Separate execution from presentation.** Return independent verdicts for PROCESS/LIFECYCLE, STATE, VIEWTREE, GEOMETRY, DRAW_OPS, BUFFER_CHANGED, PRESENTED_FRAME, CAPTURE, REAL_APP_CONTENT. Never collapse these into “success”.

**06 — Fix the evidence gate before trusting it.** Parse JSON structurally, not with fragile regexes; add a synthetic test where escaped text, zero-valued dimensions and legitimate caught exceptions cannot produce false PASS/FAIL.

**07 — Make a first-divergence pair report.** Compare a working target and a white target side by side; show the first stage where their paths differ, rather than dumping two huge logs.

**08 — Use a fast two-pass schedule.** Pass 1: cheap source search, logs, tree/geometry and targeted probes. Pass 2: only for top high-fan-out roots, run full 3-run/corpus validation. Save full expensive runs for hypotheses that survived Pass 1.

### B. Window, ViewTree, measure and layout (9–18)

**09 — Verify window root attachment.** Trace decor/content root identity from Activity.setContentView to the actual render traversal. If Activity and content exist but no root reaches traversal, fix the generic attach contract, not the app.

**10 — Audit setContentView overloads.** XML layout ID, direct View, null/replacement, repeated calls and content-parent reuse must all converge on one correct root contract.

**11 — Recheck MeasureSpec encoding/decoding.** Validate mode and size bit masks for EXACTLY, AT_MOST and UNSPECIFIED, including zero-sized specs; compare against AOSP tests/source.

**12 — Recheck getChildMeasureSpec full table.** MATCH_PARENT/WRAP_CONTENT/fixed sizes across every parent mode, padding and margins. Add table-driven probes for all combinations and prove expected measured dimensions.

**13 — Recheck resolveSizeAndState.** UNSPECIFIED must preserve desired size; EXACTLY obeys parent size; AT_MOST clamps correctly; measured-state bits must not corrupt dimensions.

**14 — Recheck LinearLayout weight distribution.** Height/width=0 with weight, remaining-space calculation, negative/overflow space, padding, margins, gravity and weighted children. This is a known prior Telegram root; test current HEAD rather than reimplementing it blindly.

**15 — Recheck ConstraintLayout solver parity.** Revalidate F-NEW-451/F-NEW-453 and its 23-node keypad subtree result. Add independent constraints (baseline, chains, guidelines, gone margins, min/max) and cross-app fixtures to detect a one-screen-only correction.

**16 — Audit stale DEX-vs-native measured dimensions.** If DEX and native paths both write measuredWidth/Height, define a single authoritative write/read contract, generation/validity, and invalidation. Prevent old 0x0 values from overwriting a later valid measurement.

**17 — Verify late attachment and second traversal.** A child attached after initial measure must trigger the correct parent-derived specs and a subsequent traversal. Test attach/detach, visibility changes, add/remove, requestLayout and invalidate separately.

**18 — Verify clipping, scroll and off-screen geometry.** Record parent/child bounds, scroll offsets, clip bounds and visible intersection. Detect “tree has nodes but every meaningful child is outside the frame” without forcing them on-screen.

### C. Drawing, text, drawable and frame production (19–28)

**19 — Separate draw dispatch from canvas capture.** Record whether draw/onDraw/dispatchDraw executed, how many canvas calls the app issued, how many the bridge captured, and how many operations reached the renderer. These are different counters.

**20 — Audit Canvas bridge method coverage.** Compare methods called by actual DEX traces against implemented CanvasShadow overloads: save/restore, translate/scale/rotate, clip, drawColor, rect/roundRect, path, bitmap, text, paint, alpha and matrices. Prioritize methods with observed callers, not a blind API inventory.

**21 — Prove draw operations reach pixels.** For a known test shape, trace operation → transformed/clipped bounds → raster write → final buffer hash. A positive draw-op count with unchanged buffer is a failure, not success.

**22 — Revalidate debug placeholders/fills.** Ensure C013/GREY_200 debug surfaces remain opt-in or correctly conditional and cannot hide app content. A fallback frame must have a distinct verdict such as DIAGNOSTIC_PLACEHOLDER, never REAL_APP_CONTENT.

**23 — Audit sibling order and overlay surfaces.** Verify parent-before-child order, sibling order, custom child order, Z/elevation and full-screen siblings. Test a late overlay with a small known child to reveal overpaint.

**24 — Audit invalidation and frame scheduling.** Verify invalidate()/postInvalidate() marks the correct damage, schedules a frame and does not leave an app permanently at its initial/splash state. Distinguish “draw was skipped because no damage” from “draw path broken”.

**25 — Audit TextView baseline and glyph path.** Trace text object → layout/line boxes → baseline → paint/font → clipping → raster pixels. Check non-ASCII, empty text, spans, gravity, ellipsize and long strings.

**26 — Audit background/drawable materialization.** Verify setBackground/setBackgroundDrawable, GradientDrawable shape+color, StateListDrawable state selection, bounds, intrinsic dimensions, alpha and mutation. Prior Telegram evidence names a programmatic GradientDrawable/FAB gap; revalidate before fixing.

**27 — Audit ImageView/BitmapFactory end to end.** Decode source bytes to a real bitmap, preserve width/height/config/pixels, apply scaleType/matrix/padding, then prove pixels appear at expected destination bounds. Do not confuse successful resource lookup with successful bitmap drawing.

**28 — Audit density, transforms and insets.** Use one coordinate-space contract for dp↔px, canvas matrices, view translation/scale, status/navigation insets and screenshot coordinates. Verify click coordinates map to the same visual object.

### D. Telegram: from “runs” to actual usable UI (29–38)

**29 — Fresh official Telegram run from current HEAD.** Use the official APK and installed identity, fresh data root, fixed viewport and recorded APK/binary SHA. Do not substitute Forkgram results for official Telegram; use Forkgram only as a comparative twin.

**30 — Revalidate startup and first screen.** Trace LaunchActivity → lifecycle → fragment stack → content root → measure/layout/draw. Separate uncaught errors=0 from real visual completion.

**31 — Finish the real intro/login frame.** Check logo/TextureView, title, subtitle, button background, dimensions and all meaningful children. Require actual app pixels and ViewTree provenance, not a lower color count alone.

**32 — Fix the country-picker attachment path.** Prior evidence says the picker fragment's create lifecycle ran but its tree did not attach. Trace fragment transaction → parent/fragment container → attach → measure → draw; identify the exact first missing link and fix the generic fragment/container law.

**33 — Fix the country/phone input row.** Prior evidence reported a second-pass 0x0 child. Trace child creation, LayoutParams, parent measure specs, EditText/TextView dimensions, focus and input dispatch; prove typed digits update the real UI state and frame.

**34 — Revalidate login button hit target and state transition.** Tap the measured bounds of the actual button, prove the real listener ran, and record fragment/navigation state plus the next frame. No coordinate-only scripted navigation shortcut.

**35 — Revalidate login→main navigation.** Trace fragment replacement/back stack, lifecycle callbacks, attachment and invalidation. Detect “destination created but old face remains” separately from navigation failure.

**36 — Fix RecyclerView/ViewHolder row construction.** Existing Telegram notes report database content without constructed rows. Trace adapter item count → create/bind ViewHolder → LayoutParams → measure/layout → draw; test a generic adapter fixture plus Telegram. Do not fabricate rows.

**37 — Verify dialog row tap → chat handoff.** Once rows exist, prove row identity/position → dialog data → real chat fragment → visible header/message area. Record state mutation and hit target, not just click dispatch.

**38 — Build a short user-journey gate.** Automate cold start → Start Messaging → country picker → phone entry → next/login state; add main/dialogs/chat steps only when prerequisites pass. Each step must assert tree, geometry, state and rendered frame; report exact frontier if blocked.

### E. Compose, async work and broader apps/games (39–45)

**39 — Trace Dooz/Compose first divergence.** Follow Activity → ComposeView → composition → Applier/ComposeNode → LayoutNode → measure/place → draw → frame. Use current F-NEW-445..453 registry and current source; do not port an entire Compose runtime without proof.

**40 — Test recomposition and state observation.** Change a state value after initial composition and prove the correct node updates and the frame changes. A composed initial tree with no state-driven update is not interactive compatibility.

**41 — Audit Handler/Looper/frame callback delivery.** Record enqueue/dequeue, thread, delay, callback and cancellation. Detect a traversal/recomposition/frame callback that is queued but never executed, or runs on an invalid thread.

**42 — Audit async content attachment.** For data arriving after first frame, prove callback → adapter/state update → requestLayout/invalidate/recompose → next frame. Check ordering and teardown races.

**43 — Preserve SurfaceView/GL/native game paths.** Ensure a View-family diagnostic/fallback renderer never replaces a surface/GL composite. Use a real 2D Canvas game and a surface/GL game as controls; do not count a skeleton/outline as gameplay rendering.

**44 — Revalidate WebView/HTML5 separately.** Distinguish WebView creation, DOM readiness, JavaScript execution, canvas/game loop, compositing and capture. Use existing Breakout evidence as a control, but verify current HEAD.

**45 — Run five concrete cross-family examples.** Select at least five currently reproducible apps/games across View, messaging, Compose, WebView and game/surface families. For each state: “fails at X; source contract is Y; shared fix is Z; affected peers are A/B; falsifying test is T.”

### F. High-fan-out fixes, regression and truthful completion (46–50)

**46 — Cluster before coding.** Group the findings from tasks 1–45 into root-cause clusters (attachment, measurement, invalidation/frame scheduling, canvas capture, fragment navigation, RecyclerView, Compose state, surface composition). Implement one shared semantic fix per proven cluster where possible.

**47 — Add minimal synthetic probes for each fixed law.** Probe both the failing case and a negative/control case; include edge cases that would have exposed the bug. Do not add new roots for already-covered semantics—update their existing evidence.

**48 — Run A/B and regression on current binary.** For every generic fix, compare baseline and candidate with identical APK/data/viewport/environment. Run relevant golden games and working apps; investigate every hash drift. Repeat three times for important targets and compare cold/warm where relevant.

**49 — Update one durable evidence ledger.** Update #366/#372 or the appropriate existing Telegram issue and synchronize the root registry/worklog/evidence paths. Record current source SHA, APK SHA, binary hash, commands, traces, ViewTree provenance, dimensions, screenshot SHA, actual state transitions, regression results and status.

**50 — Deliver a prioritized verdict, not 50 “done” labels.** Final report: top shared root causes ranked by impact × confidence; code locations and proposed/implemented fixes; which apps visibly improved; which journey steps now work; exact still-open first divergences; test commands/results; regressions; commits and verified remote HEAD. Leave #364 open while any required row is PARTIAL/BLOCKED/PENDING.

## Required execution order (to save time)
1. Start with tasks 01–08 and reuse #366's differential matrix.
2. In parallel, investigate clusters 09–18 and 19–28 using the same selected targets.
3. Use Telegram tasks 29–38 as the high-value real-app journey, but do not bypass a generic root.
4. Run Compose/surface/WebView checks 39–45 against their actual execution families.
5. Only then implement grouped fixes, synthetic probes and regression (46–50).

## Acceptance gate
A successful cycle is **not** 50 checkboxes. It is: first divergence proven for the selected real APKs; a small number of shared runtime laws corrected; at least five actual app/game cases retested; Telegram's real tree/interaction/frame journey measurably advances; working controls do not regress; current-head evidence is reproducible. If no source-level bug is confirmed for a candidate, mark it ALREADY_COVERED / BLOCKED / NOT_APPLICABLE and explain why—do not invent a fix.

AOSP reference for MeasureSpec/requestLayout/invalidate/draw semantics: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/HEAD/core/java/android/view/View.java
AOSP traversal reference: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/ViewRootImpl.java
Compose lifecycle/recomposition references: https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/lifecycle and https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/quick-guides/content/video/debugging-recomposition

- **V1 probe refutes the old theory:** the CONT-113 "ctor this-binding" hypothesis was tested first (fixtures/c114_f462_probe, real aapt2/ECJ/D8): a Gfx ctor that creates a GLSurfaceView-subclass view then stores its own fields kept ALL fields correct pre-fix (`[C462-SELF] app_null=false cfg_null=false view_null=false lft=77`). Theory REFUTED, honestly.
- **True root (fresh trace):** all 11 `[IGET-MISS-DIAG]` rows on obj#138 (heap class GLSurfaceView20) have `caller=AndroidGraphics.onDrawFrame` — the frame pump `dispatch_gl_surface_view_frame` passed the **VIEW object** as args[0] of `onSurfaceCreated`/`onSurfaceChanged`/`onDrawFrame` while dispatching the **renderer's** class methods. AOSP law (GLSurfaceView.GLThread.guardedRun): the callbacks run ON the renderer installed by setRenderer.
- **Fix:** one line — bind args[0] to the renderer object stored in the view's `glRenderer` field.
- **Bracket:** probe V2 rows pre-fix 0/3 (ctorStamp/seq read 0 on every callback) → post-fix 3/3 (`ctorStamp=777`, `seq=4242`, 6 frames, exit 0→0). Tower3d: obj#138 misses 11 → **0**; setupGL now completes (`Gdx.app` stored at pc=85, past the old pc=29/pc=7 NPEs).

- **F-NEW-497 ROOT-CAUSED-FIXED — POST-CAPTURE DRAIN-TO-DEADLINE:** بعد از حلقه فریم‌ها، تا وقتی کار آینده‌دار در صف هست و ساعت مجازی < بودجه اعلام‌شده (`--max-seconds`): پیشروی poll-timeout (پاریتی AOSP MessageQueue.next)، تخلیه و اجرای Runnable ها از همان مسیر قانونی، pump بامزه per-boundary، و مصرف `pending_intent` در **هر** مرز (نسخه اول آبشار GameActivity را بعد از اسکرین‌شات رها می‌کرد — اصلاح شد). قطعی (صفر ساعت دیواری)، یکنواخت (بدون چک اپ‌خاص)، قرارداد launch-frame دست‌نخورده. سقف §18: ۵۱۲ دور / ۶۴ دور بی‌پیشرفت.

# CONT-159 — «ادامه» — موج کشف ریشهٔ tower3d + ۸ قانون موتوری

**پایان:** HEAD `980dabd2` (pushed، HEAD==origin/main تأیید شد)، باینری `2acd3a23e7064f2c`، رجیستری **۸۲۲ ریشه** (id-unique، main==mirror).

## سؤال این موج
مرز صادق CONT-158 می‌گفت: tower3d (چهرهٔ سیاه یکنواخت — کشف معلق)، chess (زنجیرهٔ getxml)، dooz×2 (دیوار throughput از F084)، tictactoe (مرز libGDX/native). این موج به سراغ tower3d رفت — و زنجیرهٔ کشتن کامل کشف و تعمیر شد: **۸ قانون موتوری عمومی** در یک نشست.

## زنجیرهٔ کشف (با مدرک بایت-سطح)
1. **F-NEW-500** — `String.compareTo` اصلاً وجود نداشت؛ fallback بی‌جواب ۰ می‌داد ⇒ `Attribute.register` در libGDX **همهٔ alias‌ها را به بیت ۱ فرو ریخت** (`DirectionalLightsAttribute.Type == ColorAttribute.Type == 1`) ⇒ `Environment.add` با کلیدِ DLA یک ColorAttribute بیگانه را مچ کرد. دستاورد پس از فیکس: `DLA.Type = 128` (بیت یکتا).
2. **F-NEW-501** — مادیالایزر R414 بدون descriptor فراخوانی می‌کرد؛ قانون EXP-078 (بایت‌کد بزرگ‌تر برنده) **کپی‌سازندهٔ Array** را به‌جای `()V` اجرا کرد (۳۰ یونیت > ۷) ⇒ `getClass()` روی `items` غایب پوستهٔ تازه ⇒ NPE.
3. **F-NEW-502** — `Class.getComponentType` غایب ⇒ `Array.newInstance(null,…)` ⇒ NPE در `resize`.
4. **F-NEW-503** — پل GLES20 با اندیسِ «آرگومان جاوا» روی آرایهٔ pointer-only کار می‌کرد ⇒ `glGenBuffers` از طریق nullptr نوشت ⇒ **SIGSEGV fault=0x0** (اولین عنوان libGDX-3D که به mesh رسید). + **503b**: `glGetShaderiv` غایب ⇒ `isCompiled()=0` ⇒ IAE در `createDefaultShader`.
5. **F-NEW-504** — native های کلاس-اپ هرگز به bridge_to_api نمی‌رسیدند ⇒ libgdx.so واقعی fault شد (محافظت‌شده) ⇒ null ⇒ NPE در `order()`. + شادوی `newDisposableByteBuffer`.
6. **F-NEW-505** — `portablegl.h:15223` ستاب است: `glCreateShader → return 0` ⇒ `loadShader` کامپایل را رد کرد ⇒ IAE. فیکس: ضرب‌کردن handle واقعی سمت موتور + نقشهٔ location پایدار.
7. **F-NEW-506** — write-back خروجی gen* غایب بود ⇒ «No buffer allocated!».
8. **F-NEW-507** — `getResourceAsStream` غایب ⇒ فونت پیش‌فرض libGDX نخواند شد. فیکس: بکینگ `apk-entry:` — readLine سطرهای واقعی `lsans-15.fnt` را می‌دهد.

tower3d از «چهرهٔ سیاه + ۳ زنجیرهٔ مرگ موتوری» به **اجرا عمیق اپ** رسید (SpriteBatch + Mesh + بافرهای GL + پایپ‌لاین فونت؛ آمار stub-census از ۸۴۱ به **۱۵۲۰ IMPLEMENTED**).
